concerns.text: Task T074 proposes a 'fixed-effects-only' fallback (statsmodels.GLS) if the LMM fails to converge. This directly violates Spec FR-003 ('System MUST fit a linear mixed-effects model... including random intercepts') and Constitution Principle VII ('All mixed-effects models MUST pass residual normality... checks'). The task relaxes the requirement to a non-compliant model type, constituting a silent weakening of the research constraint.

Tasks T031a-d implement a bootstrap loop comparing two fixed models (exclusion vs. imputation) rather than bootstrapping the dataset samples as required by Spec FR-008 ('report whether the coefficient direction remains consistent in ≥ 80% of bootstrap samples'). The current task logic does not satisfy the statistical definition of the acceptance criterion, effectively weakening the validation requirement.

Task T075 suggests using a 'Kaggle GPU runner' if file size exceeds 6GB. This violates Spec Assumptions ('GitHub Actions free-tier runner... sufficient') and Plan Constraints ('No GPU usage'). Introducing an unauthorized infrastructure dependency constitutes a silent drift from the constitutional reproducibility constraints.

Task T005c defines `preprocess_stats.schema.yaml` but downstream tasks (T014b, T064) write JSON without enforcing this schema. This creates a gap in Constitution Principle III (Data Hygiene) and FR-002 compliance, as the schema defined in the task is not actually used to validate the output, weakening the data integrity constraint.
